rules.title: Prohibition on coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy (BMC ch. 13.63)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license or otherwise provide to Berkeley landlords a coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels, and unlawful for a landlord to use one when setting rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley residential units. Each month of violation and each unit affected is a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Ban on sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms (using nonpublic competitor data under 90 days old) for setting rents or occupancy levels
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley. A 'coordinated pricing algorithm' uses Competitor Data (nonpublic data on other properties, less than 90 days old) to recommend rents, fees, occupancy rates or other lease terms in coordination between a Berkeley landlord and its competitors, including through a third-party vendor.
rules.exemptions: Excludes (a) products that publish aggregated, anonymous rental data without recommending rents, fees or occupancy rates; (b) products used to set rent or income limits under affordable housing guidelines; (c) products used for market research for project financing, appraisals, or research, testing or training for software development. The chapter does not regulate the amount of rent a landlord may charge.
rules.interaction: Local ordinance. This document does not address state or other preemption.
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley 
landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy 
levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.conflict_note: Open question: two published effective dates exist for this ban (1 March 2026 in the ordinance text per the brief; January 2026 per an August 2026 law-firm alert). Neither effective date is stated in this capture.
rules.notes: This document states no effective date, so effective_date is null. It records only that the Council passed the ordinance to print on November 18, 2025 (first reading). The final adoption date is not stated, so adoption_date is null. Status is in_force on the assumption that the ordinance took effect before the 2026-10-01 query date under either published date. Civil remedies of up to $1,000 per violation are omitted from key_value.

rules.title: Notification of state law limitation on tenant screening fees (BMC 13.78.010)
rules.requirement: An owner who charges a screening fee must give applicants a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the state maximum fee cap, in the application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee.
rules.key_value: Must disclose the fee rights statement and the Civ. Code § 1950.6(b) maximum fee cap before collecting a screening fee
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners or agents who charge a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and to validate, review, or otherwise process a rental application for residential property in Berkeley.
rules.interaction: Implements disclosure of the state cap under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b); the dollar cap itself is set by state law.
rules.quoted_span:
When an owner or the owner’s agent gets a request to rent residential property in Berkeley from an applicant and the owner charges a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and to validate, review, or otherwise process an application, the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under
California Civil Code Section 1950.6(b)
.
rules.notes: The page gives no adoption or effective date for BMC 13.78.010, so both dates are null. The page notes the URL in the rights statement is still to be provided by the City.

rules.title: Prohibition of non-refundable application fees for existing tenancies (BMC 13.78.016)
rules.requirement: Owners may not charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, including fees tied to a roommate's departure or to adding or replacing a roommate.
rules.key_value: Ban on non-refundable renewal and roommate-change fees charged to existing tenants
rules.coverage_conditions: Existing tenants of residential rental property in Berkeley. Chapter 13.78 applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of contrary lease language (BMC 13.78.018).
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
rules.notes: The page gives no adoption or effective date for BMC 13.78.016, so both dates are null. Lease provisions that violate chapter 13.78 are unenforceable under BMC 13.78.018.

rules.title: Berkeley just cause eviction rules as amended by Measure BB
rules.requirement: Tenants in fully or partially covered units may be evicted only for just cause. Measure BB bars eviction for nonpayment unless the rental debt is at least one month of HUD Fair Market Rent for an equivalent unit, bars eviction for refusing to sign a substantially similar new fixed-term lease, and tightens lease-breach evictions.
rules.key_value: Nonpayment eviction only if rent debt is at least one month of HUD Fair Market Rent (Oakland-Fremont metro) for an equivalent-size unit
rules.coverage_conditions: Units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance, including government-owned or -subsidized units now required to register as fully or partially covered.
rules.exemptions: Exempt units are outside the ordinance. A unit where the tenant shares a kitchen or bath with the landlord is exempt only if the landlord lived on the property at the start of the tenancy.
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code ch. 13.76 (Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance), as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR as determined by the US Department of Housing and Urban Development for the fiscal year in which the rent is demanded.
rules.notes: Measure BB passed in the November 2024 election; the document states no operative date for the eviction changes, so effective_date is null. Lease-breach evictions require a material, mutually agreed term, substantial actual damage and unreasonable tenant behavior. Notices must direct tenants to the Rent Board, and copies of notices and lawsuits must be filed with the Rent Board within three business days. Owner move-in relocation assistance is adjusted for inflation annually; no amounts are given. Notice of Tenant Rights applies to tenancies started on or after 2024-12-20, which is an application date, not an effective date.

rules.title: Berkeley 2026 Annual General Adjustment (AGA), Rent Board Regulation 1148
rules.requirement: Eligible landlords may raise 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than January 1, 2026, using the AGA set at 65% of the Bay Area CPI-U increase. The Order sets qualifying conditions and tenant notice requirements.
rules.key_value: 1.0% (65% of 1.5% Bay Area CPI-U, July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025)
rules.coverage_conditions: Eligible landlords of units under Berkeley rent stabilization; the AGA may not adjust rents of tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025 whose rents were set pursuant to the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act.
rules.exemptions: Tenancies beginning on or after January 1, 2025 with rents set under Costa-Hawkins are not adjusted by the 2026 AGA.
rules.interaction: Operates under Berkeley Municipal Code 13.76.110A; Costa-Hawkins (state law) limits which tenancies the AGA reaches.
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code § 13.76.110(A); Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board Regulation 1148
rules.quoted_span: The 2026 AGA of 1.0% represents 65% of the increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for All Urban Consumers in the Bay Area during the period from July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025, which was 1.5% as posted by the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
rules.notes: Adopted at the Board's Oct. 16, 2025 meeting (notice dated Oct. 17, 2025). Effective date taken from 'no earlier than January 1, 2026', the earliest date increases may be taken; the notice does not use the word 'effective'. The 65% of CPI formula was approved by voters in Nov. 2004.

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Rental housing providers in Berkeley may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection or other decisions, and must give written notice and an opportunity to respond before taking any action based on criminal history.
rules.key_value: Ban on inquiring about or using criminal history in rental housing decisions
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental housing providers in Berkeley with respect to current or prospective tenants.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied properties (between 1-3 units) in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back per BMC 13.76.130 A.9; units occupied by existing tenant(s) seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
rules.notes: Source states only that City Council passed the ordinance on April 14, 2020; no effective date stated, so effective_date is null. Official city summary page; refer to the ordinance for details.

rules.title: Berkeley security deposit interest coverage
rules.requirement: Landlords of fully and partially covered units must pay interest on tenant security deposits; exempt unit types are not subject to the requirement.
rules.key_value: Security deposit interest required for fully and partially covered units
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to fully covered and partially covered unit types (e.g., multifamily built before 1980, new construction after June 1980, single-family homes, most condominiums, certain subsidized units).
rules.exemptions: Exempt: 'Golden Duplex'; owner shares kitchen or bath with tenant if owner lived on the property when the tenancy started; tenancies started after Nov 7, 2018 on properties where one unit is an ADU and either unit is owner-occupied; university rental units such as dormitories; nonprofit cooperatives.
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code ch. 13.76 (Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance)
rules.quoted_span: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980** Fully Covered Yes Yes Yes Yes

rules.title: [notice-only] Boston Housing Stability Notification Act
rules.requirement: A landlord or foreclosing owner ending a tenancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to Quit or notice of lease non-renewal. A copy of the notice, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, must also be sent to the City's Office of Housing Stability.
rules.key_value: Notice-of-rights requirement only; no just-cause protection
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords/foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston.
rules.exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; and in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse.
rules.interaction: Notice-only ordinance; does not limit the grounds for eviction or non-renewal under state law. A violation does not halt the eviction process.
rules.citation: Boston Municipal Code § 10-11.7 (Housing Stability Notification Act)
rules.quoted_span:
The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord
decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement.
rules.conflict_note: Notice-of-rights ordinance only; it does not restrict the grounds for eviction or non-renewal, so it is not a just-cause protection.
rules.notes: Effective date from 'The HSNA becomes effective on November 6, 2020.' The ordinance was passed in October 2020 (exact day not stated). Enforcement: warning for 1st offense, then $300 per day. Source is a city FAQ summarizing the ordinance.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy - criminal history
rules.requirement: Covered housing providers may not use a blanket ban on applicants with arrests or convictions and must review applicants case-by-case. They may not consider non-conviction arrests, judicially relieved convictions, juvenile records, or convictions more than 5 years old when determining eligibility or considering eviction.
rules.key_value: No consideration of non-conviction arrests, expunged/sealed convictions, juvenile records, or convictions over 5 years old
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or with income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy; also applied to the Office of Fair Housing and Equity Affirmative Marketing Program.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought and/or unreasonable risk of substantial harm to the safety of others; does not apply to current criminal behavior; conflicting federal or state criminal-history requirements preempt the policy.
rules.interaction: Federal or state law imposing a conflicting criminal history requirement preempts this policy.
rules.citation: Boston DND Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017)
rules.quoted_span: The Developer/Agent (Agent) agrees to not consider any of the following categories when determining housing eligibility and or considering eviction: a) Arrests that did not result in conviction. This includes dismissed charges, diversion programs, and similar non-convictions. b) Convictions that are subject to a form of judicial relief, such as expungement, sealing, and certificates for relief from disabilities. c) Juvenile records d) A conviction more than 5 years old.
rules.notes: Policy is dated February 2017 (page header); no effective date stated, so effective_date is null. Applies to funded/inclusionary housing providers by agreement, not all Boston landlords. Mitigating-factor guidance and appeals process are encouraged/'should' items, folded out.

rules.title: Boston fair housing protection for renters using rental assistance
rules.requirement: Landlords in Boston may not discriminate against renters or applicants because they use rental assistance, including refusing to accept Section 8, social security disability, or veterans vouchers.

rules.title: Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms (AB 325)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade, or to use or distribute one while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or commercial term.
rules.key_value: Ban on using or distributing a common pricing algorithm in a combination/conspiracy to restrain trade, or while coercing adoption of its recommended prices
rules.coverage_conditions: General antitrust law, not rental-specific. A 'common pricing algorithm' is any methodology, including a computer, software, or other technology, used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set, or otherwise influence a price or commercial term.
rules.exemptions: 'Person' does not include the end consumer of a product or service.
rules.interaction: Statewide; Section 16729(c) says it does not impair or limit the applicability of antitrust laws. Does not address local ordinances in this text.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
rules.notes: Approved by the Governor and filed 2025-10-06 (Chapter 338). The text gives no effective or operative date, so effective_date is null; it is treated as in_force because it was enacted well before the 2026-10-01 query date. Section 16756.1 (pleading standard: plausibility of conspiracy, no need to exclude independent action) is procedural and folded into this record. Rental housing is not mentioned in the text.

rules.title: California application screening fee cap and conditions (Civ. Code § 1950.6)
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge an application screening fee only up to actual out-of-pocket costs plus the reasonable value of time spent, and never more than $30 per applicant (CPI-adjustable). No fee may be charged when no unit is or will soon be available. The landlord must offer either first-come-first-served screening or a refund to unselected applicants, and must give an itemized receipt and a copy of any credit report.
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant, adjustable annually for CPI increases beginning January 1, 1998
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to a landlord (an owner of residential rental property) or their agent charging an applicant (including a guarantor or cosignor) to rent a residential housing unit.
rules.exemptions: Not intended to preempt provisions or regulations governing deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs. A landlord may accept a reusable screening report under Section 1950.1. No refund is required for an applicant denied after consideration for failing established screening criteria. The fee is not treated as an 'advance fee' or as 'security'.
rules.interaction: Applies notwithstanding Section 1950.5 (security deposits); the fee is not considered 'security' under that section. Does not preempt federal or state housing assistance program rules on deposits and fees.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
rules.notes: The document does not state when the $30 cap first took effect. The only date tied to the cap is the CPI adjustment 'beginning on January 1, 1998', so effective_date is null. The section is shown as amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67, Sec. 29 (AB 1170), effective 2026-01-01. The text does not show that the amendment changed the key value, so the date was not reset. The current CPI-adjusted dollar figure is not given in the document.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act - just cause for termination
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months, the owner may terminate only for a stated at-fault or no-fault just cause. For no-fault terminations the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 12 months' occupancy; no-fault relocation = 1 month's rent (or waiver of final month's rent)
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenant has occupied for 12 months (or 24 months if an additional adult tenant was added before an existing tenant reached 24 months, unless all tenants have 12+ months or one has 24+ months). Applies to residential real property generally, except as exempted.
rules.exemptions: Transient/tourist hotels; nonprofit hospital, religious, extended-care and licensed care facilities; school dormitories; shared bathroom/kitchen with owner-occupant; owner-occupied single-family homes renting no more than two units or bedrooms; owner-occupied duplex; housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years; separately alienable property (e.g. single-family home) not owned by a REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member, with written exemption notice; deed-restricted affordable housing; mobilehome owners.
rules.interaction: Does not apply to property covered by a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before 2019-09-01, or a later local ordinance that is more protective (with a binding local finding); property is never subject to both. A less protective local ordinance adopted after 2019-09-01 is not enforced.
rules.quoted_span: (a) Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.notes: Effective date taken from subd. (m): 'This section shall become operative on April 1, 2024.' The section as amended by AB 1529 (Stats. 2025, ch. 203) is stated to be effective 2026-01-01; it did not change the headline requirement, so the date was not reset to that. The original Tenant Protection Act start date is not stated in this text. The section is repealed as of 2030-01-01 by its own terms. Relocation notice must be given within the termination notice, and payment is due within 15 calendar days of service.

rules.title: Statewide rent cap (Tenant Protection Act), Civ. Code § 1947.12
rules.requirement: An owner may not raise the gross rental rate over any 12-month period by more than 5 percent plus the local percentage change in cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower. No more than two increments are allowed in a 12-month period for the same tenant. The owner must give notice of increases under Civ. Code § 827.
rules.key_value: 5% + CPI change, max 10% (whichever is lower), per 12 months; max two increases per 12 months
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property (including mobilehome park tenancies). The cap does not apply to housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome). It applies only to subsequent increases after the initial rent for a new tenancy in which no prior tenant remains. A mobilehome tenancy is covered only for increases on or after February 18, 2021.
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; dormitories owned and operated by a higher-education institution or a K-12 school; housing under a local rent or price control that restricts annual increases to less than the state cap; housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome); separately alienable property (e.g. single-family homes, condos) whose owner is not a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with a corporate member, and where the required written exemption notice was given; a duplex in which the owner occupies one unit as a principal residence (neither unit an ADU or JADU); homeowners of a mobilehome.
rules.interaction: Does not expand or limit local governments' authority to adopt rent control under Civ. Code ch. 2.7 (§ 1954.50 et seq.). Housing under a stricter local rent control that limits annual increases to less than the state cap is exempt from this section, so the stricter local rule controls.
rules.quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
rules.notes: Section was repealed and re-added by SB 567 (Stats. 2023, ch. 290), effective 2024-01-01 and operative 2024-04-01 by its own terms (subd. (n)). The section is repealed as of 2030-01-01 (subd. (o)). The document states the operative date of this version only. The original 2020 enactment date is not stated in this text, and the March 15, 2019 date is a look-back application date, not an effective date. The reviewer may want to confirm whether the original-requirement effective date (2020-01-01) should be used instead. The cost-of-living index is the applicable metro CPI-U, with different April comparisons before and after August 1.

rules.title: Source-of-income discrimination ban and subsidy-tenant credit/income screening limits (FEHA)
rules.requirement: Owners may not discriminate against or harass a rental applicant or tenant because of source of income, which includes Section 8 and other housing vouchers and public assistance. Where a government rent subsidy applies, income standards must be based on the tenant's portion of rent, and applicants must be allowed to offer alternative evidence in place of credit history.
rules.key_value: Ban on source-of-income discrimination (incl. Section 8 / HUD-VASH vouchers); landlords may still ask about the level or source of income
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to owners of any housing accommodation; the credit-history and income-standard rules in subd. (o) apply only where there is a government rent subsidy.
rules.exemptions: Inquiring about the level or source of income is not discrimination; landlords may still verify employment, request landlord references and verify identity.
rules.interaction: Statewide floor; this excerpt does not address local source-of-income ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person.
rules.notes: Effective date is from the document's amendment note (Stats. 2023, Ch. 776, SB 267, eff. Jan. 1, 2024), which added the subsidy-tenant credit-history alternative-evidence rule and the HUD-VASH voucher language. The document does not state when the source-of-income ban was first added, so the date reflects the amendment. Subdivisions (n), (o) and (p) are folded into this record.

rules.title: California residential security deposit cap and return rules (Civ. Code § 1950.5)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security in excess of one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent. The landlord must return the deposit with an itemized statement within 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates, and may not label any deposit 'nonrefundable'.
rules.key_value: Maximum deposit of 1 month's rent (2 months' rent for qualifying small landlords)
rules.coverage_conditions: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling. The two-month cap applies if the landlord is a natural person or an LLC whose members are all natural persons, and owns no more than two residential rental properties that collectively include no more than four dwelling units offered for rent.
rules.exemptions: Advance payment of not less than six months' rent is allowed if the lease term is six months or longer. The two-month small-landlord cap does not apply if the prospective tenant is a service member. The cap does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024.
rules.interaction: Statewide rule. The document does not address local ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
rules.notes: Section last amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340 (AB 414), effective 2026-01-01; that amendment did not change the cap. The one-month cap's own start date is not stated in this text. Subdivision (c)(6) gives only an application date (security collected before July 1, 2024 is not covered), which is not an effective date, so effective_date is null. Photograph duties: tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025 (g)(1); return photographs from April 1, 2025 (g)(2). Service-member higher-deposit rules from April 1, 2025.

rules.title: [notice-only] Tenants Rights and Resources Notification Ordinance (Cambridge M.C. ch. 8.71)
rules.requirement: Owners, landlords and management companies must give tenants the city's rights-and-resources Guide at the start of a tenancy and when legal steps to terminate a tenancy are taken (e.g., Notice to Quit or Summary Process). The ordinance does not limit the grounds for eviction.

rules.quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of a lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than 5% or the percentage difference between the consumer price index three months prior to the expiration or termination of the lease and three months prior to the commencement of the lease term, whichever is less.

rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not terminate covered tenancies without just cause and must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions. At-fault reasons include nonpayment, uncured lease violations, nuisance or damage, and illegal use. No-fault reasons include owner or family move-in, demolition or removal from the rental market, and government vacate orders.
rules.key_value: Eviction only for listed at-fault or no-fault just causes; relocation assistance owed for no-fault evictions
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the RSO. Applies once the tenant has lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease has expired, whichever comes first. Can apply to buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and to a property with only one single-family dwelling.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, certain cooperatives, some non-profit homeless facilities or short-term substance-abuse treatment centers, and some HACLA or government-owned properties.
rules.interaction: Applies to units not covered by the City's RSO, which has its own just cause rules. The JCO does not regulate rent increases; state AB 1482 may cap rent for covered units.

rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

rules.title: Relocation assistance for no-fault evictions under the RSO and JCO
rules.requirement: Landlords evicting for a tenant not-at-fault reason must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before serving notice, and must pay relocation assistance per unit within 15 days of serving the notice. Amounts depend on eligible or qualified status, length of tenancy and income.
rules.key_value: Eligible tenant: $11,000 (<3 yrs) / $14,400 (3+ yrs or low income); Qualified tenant: $23,150 / $27,400; one month's rent for JCO single-family dwellings owned by natural persons. Valid July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or Just Cause Ordinance (JCO). Qualified tenant: 62 or older, handicapped or disabled, or with one or more minor dependent children. Mom & Pop reduced amounts ($10,550 eligible / $21,250 qualified) apply only for owner or family occupancy evictions where the building has four or fewer rental units and other LAMC 151.30 conditions are met.
rules.exemptions: No relocation payment when evicting a resident manager to replace with another resident manager (unless a manager-tenant with free or reduced rent only), or when hazardous conditions caused by a natural disaster, not by landlord negligence, require eviction. evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause 
Ordinance (JCO).

That amendment did not change the cap itself. Procedural duties (receipts, condition statement, records, transfer to successor, treble damages) are folded into this record.

rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: Makes it unlawful, and a violation of the NJ Antitrust Act, for rental property owners to pay for or use a coordinator's services, for coordinators to facilitate rent-restricting agreements, and for anyone to perform a coordinating function or engage in parallel pricing coordination.
rules.key_value: Ban on algorithmic rent-setting coordination (use of coordinators / algorithmic devices performing a coordinating function)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental property owners (anyone owning one or more rental residential dwelling units) and coordinators operating algorithmic revenue management software or an algorithmic device that performs a coordinating function. Residential dwelling unit excludes inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities.
rules.exemptions: Excludes spreadsheets operating without AI and requiring human analysis, and databases that only query unprocessed data. Also excludes research/statistical/testing use of information not used to set rents, free public rent estimates, equal-terms real estate brokerage databases that do not set or recommend rents, and government affordability controls.
rules.interaction: Section 6(b) prohibits municipalities from enacting ordinances that conflict with this act, except ordinances explicitly authorized or required by other law. This may preempt local algorithmic-rent ordinances such as those of Jersey City and Hoboken once effective. The act is in addition to the NJ Antitrust Act.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful and a violation of the “New Jersey Antitrust Act,” P.L.1970, c.73 (C.56:9-1 et seq.) for: a. a rental property owner, or any agent, representative, or subcontractor thereof, to receive, subscribe to, contract for, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of, the services of a coordinator; b. a coordinator to facilitate a tacit or express agreement among rental property owners that restricts competition with respect to residential dwelling units, including by performing a coordinating function;
rules.conflict_note: Possible preemption of the Jersey City and Hoboken algorithmic-rent ordinances: section 6(b) bars municipal ordinances that conflict with the act. This document does not name those ordinances or resolve whether they conflict.
rules.notes: Section 9: takes effect on the first day of the twelfth month next following enactment. Enacted (approved) July 20, 2026, so the twelfth month following is July 2027, giving 2027-07-01. Not yet effective as of the 2026-10-01 query date. Text is the first reprint (A3497 1R ACS).

rules.title: Residential rental application fee cap (P.L. 2025, c.405)
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not require an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property that exceeds $50. Violators face civil penalties and must refund the amount wrongfully charged to the applicant.
rules.key_value: $50 maximum, adjusted annually for CPI increases (NY-Northern NJ-Long Island CPI-U)
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property leased or subleased for dwelling purposes; applies to landlords and their agents.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in a one-family or two-family dwelling offered for rent; New Jersey Real Estate Commission licensees, unless the licensee is the landlord of the property.
rules.interaction: State-wide cap with no stated preemption of local rules; local ordinances are not addressed in this document.
rules.quoted_span:
shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.
rules.notes: Section 3 says the act takes effect on the first day of the fourth month next following enactment. Enactment (approval) was January 20, 2026, so the fourth month after is May, giving 2026-05-01. This is in force as of the 2026-10-01 query date. Penalties: up to $500 first offense, $750 second, $1,000 subsequent. The CPI adjustment begins January 1 of the year after enactment (2027), applies only if CPI change is greater than zero, and the Director of Consumer Affairs publishes the adjusted limit annually.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act (good cause required)
rules.requirement: A residential landlord may not evict or refuse to renew a lease, written or oral, without good cause under the Anti-Eviction Act. Possession may be recovered only through consent or court process, and a Notice to Quit is required for all good-cause evictions except nonpayment of rent.
rules.key_value: Good cause required to evict or fail to renew a residential lease
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties, including single-family homes, mobile homes and mobile home park land, apartment buildings and complexes, and rooming and boarding homes (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53 to -84).
rules.exemptions: May not apply to owner-occupied premises with two (2) or fewer rental units; does not apply to hotel or motel guests or guest houses rented to transient or seasonal tenants (except continual-residence occupants with no alternate residence); does not apply to a unit held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies it.
rules.interaction: Statewide rule; applies regardless of local rent control. Self-help evictions and lockouts are illegal.
rules.quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.
rules.notes: Effective date not stated in this document. Relocation-assistance duties are not addressed in this part of the guide. Summary of the statute found in the official DCA guide.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: good cause required for lease non-renewal
rules.requirement: Landlords of covered residential rentals may not refuse to renew a written or oral lease unless they have good cause under the Anti-Eviction Act. The good causes are listed in the guide's Eviction section (not in this part).
rules.key_value: Good cause required to refuse renewal or evict; a lease term ending is not itself a ground
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental properties generally.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (which have a separate section), motels or hotels, and transient or seasonal units.
rules.quoted_span: No landlord of residential rental properties except t hose in owner occupied two or three family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units may fail to renew any lease, regardless of whether it is written or oral unless they have good cause not to renew the lease.
rules.notes: Only the non-renewal summary appears in this part; the list of causes and any relocation-assistance duties are in later parts of the guide. The guide cites the statute as 'N.J.S.A. 2A:18:61.3'. No effective date is stated in this document.

rules.title: No statewide rent control (municipal option); rent increase notice and unconscionability standard
rules.requirement: New Jersey sets no statewide cap on rents, and municipalities may adopt their own rent control or leveling ordinances. A landlord may raise rent only by properly terminating the lease and offering a new one, and the increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with any local ordinance.
rules.key_value: No state rent cap; increases must not be unconscionable and must follow any municipal rent control ordinance
rules.coverage_conditions: Statewide; local rent control boards apply only where a municipality has adopted a rent control or leveling ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control for 30 years after completion of construction (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5); government-subsidized rents, HUD-owned/subsidized or HUD-insured developments, and NJHMFA-financed projects may also be exempt.
rules.interaction: State leaves rent regulation to municipalities; municipal ordinances (e.g. Jersey City, Hoboken, Newark) govern the allowable increases where they exist. State notice rules in the Anti-Eviction Act apply alongside local rules.
rules.quoted_span: The State of New Jersey has no laws that establish, govern or control rents.
rules.notes: Secondary summary by the state agency (DCA Truth in Renting guide). No effective date stated in this document. Increase procedure: written notice terminating the old lease and offering a new lease at the increased rent.

rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination: source of lawful income / rent payment protection
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate in housing based on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent payment, so they cannot deny a Section 8 voucher holder an apartment solely because of that income source.
rules.key_value: Ban on refusing tenants based on source of lawful income (including Section 8 vouchers)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to the sale or rental of all property, business or residential, including open land.
rules.exemptions: Rental of a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit; rental of rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling; religious-organization preference for persons of the same religion (sale/lease/rental); familial status rule does not apply to housing for older persons (N.J.S.A. 10:5-5mm).
rules.quoted_span:
The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based
on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent
or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses.
rules.notes: Secondary summary brochure (rev. 06.18.15) of the LAD; the document states no effective date for the source-of-income provision, so effective_date is null. Complaints filed with the Division within 180 days; the Division does not handle ordinary landlord-tenant disputes such as evictions.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act (criminal record screening limits)
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not inquire about an applicant's criminal record before making a conditional offer. After the offer, only certain convictions within set look-back periods may be considered, and a withdrawal requires an individualized assessment and written notice.
rules.key_value: No criminal-record inquiry before conditional offer; after offer, only convictions for listed serious offenses (no time limit) or indictable offenses within look-back periods of 6 years (1st degree), 4 years (2nd/3rd degree) and 1 year (4th degree)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to a 'rental dwelling unit', meaning a dwelling unit offered for rent by a housing provider for residential purposes, other than a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Housing providers may consider convictions for methamphetamine manufacture on the premises of federally assisted housing and lifetime sex offender registration status. Owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded.
rules.quoted_span:
A housing
provider
shall not make any oral or written inquiry
regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
rules.notes: Effective date computed from section 14: the act takes effect on the first day of the seventh month next following enactment. Enactment was June 18, 2021 (Approved June 18, 2021), so the seventh month following is January 2022, giving 2022-01-01. Also folded in: written disclosure before accepting any application fee (s.4b), no evaluation of arrests without conviction, expunged or sealed records (s.5a), and a ban on requiring drug or alcohol tests (s.9). Enforcement is through the Division on Civil Rights, with penalties up to $1,000, $5,000 or $10,000.)

rules.title: NJ Security Deposit Law: cap of 1.5 months' rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit above one and one-half times one month's rent, and prepaid rent held as security (including last month's rent) counts toward that cap. Deposits must be held in trust in an interest-bearing account, with interest going to the tenant, and returned within 30 days after the tenancy ends.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent maximum; annual increases limited to 10% of the current deposit
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (a tenant there may opt in 30 days after a written request to the landlord). The interest-account rules do not apply to seasonal rentals of not more than 125 consecutive days.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ).
rules.notes: Secondary DCA guide summarizing the statute; no effective date is stated in this document. The guide also says a pet deposit combined with the regular deposit cannot exceed 1.5 months' rent, and that the landlord may require only the first month's rent in addition to the deposit (max 2.5 months' rent at lease inception). Return deadline: 30 days, with an itemized list of deductions sent by registered or certified mail.}},{

rules.title: NJ Security Deposit Act: application of act
rules.requirement: The state security deposit act applies to all rental premises or units used for dwelling purposes. Owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units are covered only where the tenant gives the landlord 30 days written notice invoking the act.
rules.key_value: Applies to all dwelling rentals; owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units only after 30 days written tenant notice
rules.coverage_conditions: All rental premises or units used for dwelling purposes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units where the tenant has failed to provide 30 days written notice to the landlord invoking the act.
rules.quoted_span: The provisions of this act shall apply to all rental premises or units used for dwelling purposes except owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units where the tenant has failed to provide 30 days written notice to the landlord invoking the provisions of this act.
rules.conflict_note: Secondary source (secondary (law firm / news / mirror)); confirm against the official text.
rules.notes: This is a scope section only. The deposit cap, interest and return rules are in other sections (46:8-19 et seq.) and are not in this document. Effective date set to null: the only dates are in the history note (L.1967, c. 265, eff. Jan. 1, 1968, with later amendments), which I did not treat as a stated effective date for the requirement. Secondary mirror (Justia, 2025 version) with a disclaimer that it may not be current.

rules.title: Newark Rent Control - limitation on increases (25% ceiling) and exemptions
rules.requirement: The Rent Control Board may not grant any tenant rent increases exceeding 25% in any one year, counting regular, major-improvement and hardship increases within the prior 12 months. Other ceilings apply to utilities surcharges and vacant-unit rehabilitation increases.
rules.key_value: Board may not grant increases exceeding 25% in any one year (regular CPI-based annual increase is in § 19:2-3, not in this part)
rules.coverage_conditions: Dwellings subject to Newark's rent control chapter; rents controlled at the level received as of the chapter's first adoption on September 4, 1985, with the chapter continuing in force from October 19, 1988.
rules.exemptions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt for the lesser of the initial-mortgage amortization period or 30 years after completion (30 years if no mortgage). Vacant properties vacant 18 months and rehabilitated at over 50% of fair market value are exempt for five years. Substantially rehabilitated dwellings may set an unrestricted initial rent. Vacant-unit rehabilitation (spending at least 12 months of rent) allows a maximum 10% increase, once per 12 months. Utilities surcharge is capped at 15% of the monthly rent roll for 30 or fewer units, 5% for 31-200 units and 3% for over 200 units.
rules.quoted_span: Since an immediate rent increase of more than 25% above the prior monthly rent may be considered unconscionable and imposes a hardship on a tenant, the Rent Control Board shall not grant increases exceeding 25% in any one year for any tenant.
rules.notes: The tenant-facing annual allowable increase (§ 19:2-3) is in another part of the chapter and is not in this capture. No effective date is stated for § 19:2-22 (amended 9-18-2024 by Ord. 6PSF-I per history note); the later 5-20-2026 amendments touch other sections (vacant properties, substantial rehabilitation, fees, inspections), so effective_date is null.

rules.title: Newark Rent Control: annual CPI-based rent increase cap
rules.requirement: At lease expiration (or termination of a periodic tenancy), a landlord may not request or receive an increase greater than the CPI-U change measured from 15 months to 3 months before the month of the proposed increase, and never more than 4%. Written notice of at least 30 days must go to the tenant and the Rent Regulation Officer, and no increase is allowed unless the dwelling is in substantial compliance and the landlord has registered.
rules.key_value: CPI-U increase (NY-Northern NJ-Long Island), max 4%
rules.coverage_conditions: All multiple dwellings as defined in § 19:2-2 are subject to rent control (§ 19:2-2.1). The cap applies to any 12-month period regardless of tenant turnover, ownership change or vacancy (§ 19:2-3.2).
rules.exemptions: Public housing; hotel/motel space rented day-to-day to transients; commercial space; newly constructed multiple dwellings and vacant dwellings per §§ 19:2-18.1 and 19:2-18.2 (details not in this part); certain federal/state rehabilitated Section 8 units (rent capped at HUD fair market rent); units under a preemptive government rent-regulation contract.
rules.interaction: Municipal rent control; the tenant-facing cap is separate from tax, major new improvement and hardship surcharges, which the Rent Control Board may grant. The chapter is not shown to conflict with state law in this document.
rules.quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of the lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive an increase greater than the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the CPI 15 months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase to the CPI three months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase. In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed 4%.
rules.notes: Month of adoption; exact effective date not stated in source (NJ ordinances generally take effect after final passage and publication). Section history shows original Ord. 6 PSF-A(S) of 9-5-2017, amended 9-18-2024 by Ord. No. 6PSF-I; the text does not say which amendment set the 4% ceiling, so the 2024 date is the latest amendment. Newer Ord. 6PSF-C (06-17-2026) amends only §§ 19:2-27 and 19:2-32, not this section. Detailed exemptions in §§ 19:2-18.x are in a later part of the document.

rules.title: Newark Ban the Box - Housing (criminal record check practices)
rules.requirement: A landlord or real estate broker may inquire into or consider an applicant's criminal history only after a formal application is submitted, and only after giving written notice. Look-back is limited to 8 years for indictable convictions and 5 years for disorderly persons or ordinance convictions, plus pending charges. Arrests without conviction, expunged or sealed records and juvenile adjudications may not be considered.
rules.key_value: No criminal history inquiry until after formal application; look-back 8 years (indictable) / 5 years (disorderly persons, municipal ordinance); murder, arson, registry sex offenses and terrorism convictions may be considered regardless of when they occurred
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental, lease or sublease of real property by landlords and real estate brokers; excludes (1) a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit and (2) a room or rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling.
rules.exemptions: Prohibitions do not apply where federal or state law requires or permits consideration of criminal history (limited to those offenses and periods), or to property designated for a government program that encourages housing for people with criminal histories. Exceptions are to be interpreted narrowly.
rules.quoted_span: Inquiry into and consideration of any applicant's criminal history shall take place only after the applicant has submitted a formal application.
rules.notes: Month of adoption; exact effective date not stated in source (NJ ordinances generally take effect after final passage and publication). Adoption date 4-15-2015 is taken from the Ord. 6 PSF-B citation; the Editor's Note says the earlier Ord. 6 PSF-F (2012) was repealed by Ord. 6 PSF-B. Procedural duties folded in: 3 business days to submit evidence, adverse-action notice within 10 business days by registered mail, confidentiality, and a ban on advertisements referencing criminal history. Article 2 (City licensing) is outside scope.

rules.title: San Diego Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price Fixing (SDMC §98.1103)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license or provide an algorithmic device to a landlord, and unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
rules.key_value: Ban on selling, licensing, or using algorithmic rent-setting devices (software using nonpublic competitor data of two or more landlords)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental property in the City of San Diego; 'algorithmic device' means software that uses algorithms to calculate nonpublic competitor data of two or more landlords to recommend rental rates or occupancy levels.
rules.exemptions: Excludes software that publishes reports from aggregated historical nonpublic data more than 90 days old or public information without recommending future rates; software used to set rents or income limits under affordable housing program guidelines; appraisal software that does not recommend rental rates during runtime.
rules.interaction: No state or other-level interaction stated in this document. Remedies are cumulative with other law.
rules.citation: San Diego Municipal Code § 98.1103 (Ord. O-21955 N.S.)
rules.quoted_span:
(b) It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or  
occupancy levels for residential rental property.
rules.notes: Added 5-22-2025 by O-21955 N.S.; effective 6-21-2025 per the document. Each month of violation per property is a separate violation; tenants may seek injunctive relief, damages or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation (§98.1104). Proposal (S.D. Mun. Code § 98.1103 (proposed; Ord. O-2025-107), D076) adopted as San Diego Municipal Code § 98.1103 (Ord. O-21955 N.S.).

rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections (just cause for termination of tenancy)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a covered tenancy without at-fault or no-fault just cause. For no-fault terminations the landlord must give relocation assistance, either as a direct payment within 15 days of the notice or as a rent waiver, and must notify the Housing Commission. Buyout agreements must follow written disclosure rules and may not be for less than the relocation amount.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; no-fault relocation assistance = 2 months' actual rent (3 months if tenant is a senior 62+ or disabled)
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property with a tenancy of more than 30 days. Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years is exempt (unless a mobilehome). Separately alienable property is exempt only if the landlord is not a REIT, a corporation, an LLC with a corporate member, or a mobilehome park management, and the tenant received the required written exemption notice.
rules.exemptions: Includes transient/tourist hotels and short-term occupancy; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (but not Section 8); mobilehomes under the Mobilehome Residency Law; nonprofit hospitals, religious, care and transitional facilities; dormitories; shared-facility rentals with the landlord; owner-occupied single-family residences (up to two bedrooms or ADUs) and owner-occupied duplexes; housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years; and qualifying separately alienable property with written notice. See § 98.0703.
rules.interaction: Consistent with and additional to California Civil Code § 1946.2; the rights are in addition to any state or federal rights. Relocation assistance is credited against any other relocation assistance required by federal, state or other local law and is in addition to return of the security deposit.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause.
rules.notes: Added 5-25-2023 by O-21647 N.S.; effective 6-24-2023. Amended 2-27-2024 by O-21769 N.S., effective 3-28-2024 (§§ 98.0702, 98.0704, 98.0709, 98.0710 added or amended). The amendment text does not show a change to the headline relocation figures, so the original effective date is used. Relocation amounts are in § 98.0706(c). At-fault grounds are in § 98.0704(a) and no-fault grounds in § 98.0704(b).

rules.title: San Diego Prohibition of Discrimination Based on a Tenant's Source of Income
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to enter into or renew a tenancy, terminate a tenancy, or apply income standards that ignore a tenant's entire source of income, including rental assistance and vouchers, based on source of income. Income standards must account for aggregate income of co-tenants and cosigners on the same basis as married persons.
rules.key_value: Ban on source-of-income discrimination (includes federal, state, local or nonprofit rental assistance and subsidies)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental-units and tenancies in the City of San Diego as defined in Municipal Code section 98.0720.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply where the owner or a family member resides in the same residential building and shares a bathroom or kitchen facility with the tenant or prospective tenant (§98.0804). Acts necessary to comply with program requirements related to source of income are excepted.
rules.interaction: Defines source of income more broadly than the California FEHA definition; landlords keep the right to reject applicants for other lawful reasons consistent with federal, state and local law.
rules.citation: San Diego Municipal Code §§ 98.0801-98.0806 (Ord. O-20986 N.S.)
rules.quoted_span:
It is unlawful for any person to do any of the following acts, wholly or in 
part, based on a person’s source of income  (except as may be necessary to 
comply with any program requirements related to source of income ):
rules.notes: Division added 9-18-2018 by O-20986 N.S.; effective 10-18-2018. Remedies (§98.0806) include treble one month's rent in damages for violations on or after August 1, 2019, plus injunction and fees; not used as key value.

rules.title: S.F. Rent Ordinance Section 37.10C - Prohibition on Algorithmic Rent-Setting Devices
rules.requirement: Prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices (software that analyzes nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents for vacant units) to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units. Tenants or the City Attorney may bring a civil action for violations.
rules.key_value: Ban on sale or use of algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential units in San Francisco; 'algorithmic device' means a device such as a software program that uses algorithms to analyze nonpublic competitor rental data for the purposes of providing a landlord recommendations on what rent to charge for a vacant unit.
rules.quoted_span: The law prohibits the sale or use of such algorithmic devices and allows a tenant or the City Attorney to bring a civil action if they believe an entity is in violation of the law.
rules.notes: Secondary summary from the SF Rent Board news page; effective date stated in the text as October 14, 2024. The text does not give the ordinance number; citation follows the Section 37.10C reference in the Rent Ordinance (S.F. Admin. Code ch. 37).

rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance just cause eviction (S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9(a))
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance only for a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for the eviction; 17 enumerated reasons are allowed, and expiration of a lease or change in ownership is not just cause.
rules.key_value: Eviction only for one of 17 enumerated just causes (Section 37.9(a))
rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the Rent Ordinance, including some units exempt from rent increase limits: newly constructed units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, tenancies eligible for a rent increase under Costa-Hawkins, and some tenancies where rent is regulated by another government agency.
rules.interaction: Applies even to some tenancies exempt from the Ordinance's rent increase limits (e.g., Costa-Hawkins-exempt units); state just cause law is not discussed in this document.
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.
rules.notes: Official SF Rent Board summary page; effective date not stated in the document, so null. Relocation-assistance amounts are not covered in this document.

rules.title: San Francisco annual allowable rent increase (3/1/2026\u20132/28/2027)
rules.requirement: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable rent increase effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6% of the tenant's base rent.
rules.key_value: 1.6% annual allowable increase (3/1/2026\u20132/28/2027)
rules.coverage_conditions: Rent-controlled units in San Francisco subject to the Rent Ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.
rules.notes: Announcement of the annual figure; the prior year's (3/1/2025\u20132/28/2026) figure was 1.4%. Example: $2,000 base rent x .016 = $32 increase. Citation to the Rent Ordinance is inferred; the page does not cite a section.

rules.title: Fair Chance Ordinance (affordable housing)
rules.requirement: San Francisco's Fair Chance Ordinance protects residents with arrest or conviction history in affordable housing decisions. This page gives no operative details beyond that statement.
rules.key_value: Protection against use of arrest or conviction history in affordable housing decisions
rules.coverage_conditions: Affordable housing decisions only, per the page's description; no thresholds are stated.
rules.citation: S.F. Police Code art. 49 (Fair Chance Ordinance)
rules.quoted_span: San Francisco's Fair Chance Ordinance protects residents with arrest or conviction history in affordable housing decisions.
rules.notes: Navigation or teaser text on an agency landing page. The citation comes from general knowledge, not this document. The page states no effective date, adoption date or specific requirements, so effective_date is null.

rules.title: SF security deposit interest rate
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay interest on tenant security deposits at the Rent Board rate, which is 4.2% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027.
rules.key_value: 4.2% interest for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies subject to San Francisco's security deposit interest rules; thresholds are not stated in this document.
rules.quoted_span: 4.2% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027
rules.notes: Prior rates were 5.0% (3/1/25–2/28/26) and 5.2% (3/1/24–2/28/25). The citation is not given in this document and is supplied from knowledge of the SF Administrative Code.

rules.title: Santa Ana Ordinance NS-3090 (automated rent price-fixing)
rules.requirement: Santa Ana prohibits specified anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing, and tenants may bring private claims.
rules.key_value: Ban on automated rent price-fixing
rules.quoted_span: Ordinance NS-3090 prohibits specified anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing; private tenant claims and up to $1,000 per violation and per month.
rules.conflict_note: Secondary source (secondary (law firm / news / mirror)); confirm against the official text.
rules.notes: Secondary source. Effective date from the table ('effective April 2, 2026'). Municipal code section not given in the document. Proposal (Santa Ana Municipal Code, algorithmic rent-setting software ordinance (ordinance number and section not stated in source), D087) adopted as Santa Ana Ordinance No. NS-3090.

rules.title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: After 30 days of tenancy, an owner may not terminate a tenancy without just cause stated in a written notice. For no-fault terminations the owner must give 3 months of relocation assistance or waive rent for the final 3 months.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 30 days; no-fault termination requires 3 months relocation assistance or 3 months rent waiver
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies generally; protection begins after the first 30 days of tenancy.
rules.exemptions: Housing produced in the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing; hotel and transient occupancy; hospital and care facilities; dormitories; and other shared living quarters.

rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance
rules.requirement: Annual residential rent increases are capped at the lower of 3% or 80% of the CPI change over the most recent 12 months; no increase is allowed if CPI is negative. The City publishes the allowable increase by June 30 each year, effective September 1.
rules.key_value: Lower of 3% per year or 80% of CPI change (12 months); no increase if CPI negative
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental units; the cap does not apply to residential buildings constructed after February 1, 1995, or to mobile home spaces offered for rent after January 1, 1990.
rules.exemptions: Owners may petition the City Manager or designee for relief from the cap by showing a larger increase is necessary for a fair and reasonable return; decision within 60 days of a complete application.
